audit.why: Emerald+ 48.78% over 3073 games — the largest sample in the slice and genuinely below even, which matches both charts giving Jayce only Levels 2-3 and the first-item window against a tank who never falls off. The page already frames it as a cooldown war over Dredge Line rather than a lane Jayce simply wins.

Level 6 is correctly given to Nautilus: Jayce's R is the stance-swap he already had, while Depth Charge is a 120s homing knockup at 825 range that chains into the Staggering Blow root. The scaling call is also right — Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield with no rank scaling on cooldown, so his sustain in lane comes from uptime and stacked resistances rather than a spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[1].text` and `mid` both say to 'swap to Hammer for the armor/MR shred on the first hit'. The direction is backwards.
audit.why: Riot: from Hammer Stance the swap becomes Mercury Cannon and 'the first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist'; from Cannon Stance it becomes Mercury Hammer and that first attack 'deals additional magic damage'. The shred is the first attack after swapping INTO Cannon. Against a tank stacking armour and MR this is the single most valuable button Jayce has, and the page tells the player to press it on the wrong half of a 6-second toggle — so the one combo written out twice on the page lands zero shred.
audit.corrected: The shred is the first attack after swapping into Mercury Cannon; the Hammer first hit is bonus magic damage instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line is the ability the whole page is built around, but its range and cooldown are never given, and its terrain behaviour is not mentioned at all.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 1150 range on 14/13/12/11/10. The range matters because the page repeatedly says to poke 'from outside Dredge Line range' without saying where that is — 1150 is further than most players assume, and a Jayce who thinks he is safe at 900 is not. The cooldown matters because 14 seconds at rank 1 is the actual trading window the page keeps gesturing at. And Riot's text adds that colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it, so a missed hook into a wall is not a whiff — it is a gap-close, which changes whether baiting it near terrain is safe.
audit.corrected: 1150 range, 14s at rank 1, and a hook into terrain pulls him to the wall instead of whiffing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block names Dredge Line as matchup-defining and then gives no number for it or anything else.
audit.why: The three numbers that decide every commit are Dredge Line 14s at rank 1, Titan's Wrath a flat 12s at every rank, and Thundering Blow 20s at rank 1. Titan's Wrath being flat is the non-obvious one: it does not get shorter as he levels, so the shield window stays the same all lane while his hook cooldown drops to 10s, which is why the lane gets harder to trade in over time even though nothing visible changes.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line 14s, Titan's Wrath flat 12s at all ranks, Thundering Blow 20s.

edits.before: Nautilus has to walk up to last-hit, so punish every step with the accelerated gate-Q — fire Shock Blast through your Acceleration Gate and it out-ranges anything he can answer with at level 1-3. The one thing you must dodge is Dredge Line: if his hook lands you eat the Staggering Blow root and a free trade, so weave and never sit in the obvious orb-line he's reading. Take Cannon at 1, get E by 2-3, and bully his step-ups; his only sustain is base stats and a single Titan's Wrath, and he simply has no way to poke you back at gate-Q range.
edits.after: Nautilus has to walk up to last-hit, so punish every step with the accelerated gate-Q — fire Shock Blast through your Acceleration Gate and it out-ranges anything he answers with at level 1-3. The one thing you must dodge is Dredge Line, and know where it actually reaches: 1150 units, further than most players stand. If it lands you eat the Staggering Blow root and a free trade. Do not bait it beside a wall either — a hook into terrain pulls him to the wall instead of whiffing, so the miss is still a gap-close. His only sustain is a flat-12s Titan's Wrath.
